newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts divided on outlook for Siemens.
newsitem.headline: Analysts divided on outlook for Siemens.

text.p: Siemens AG has enjoyed a 59 percent rise in its share price so far this year, but still hasn't convinced some analysts profits are also set to soar.

While Siemens points to steady cost-cutting, international expansion and a goal of 15 percent return on equity by 2000, a group of analysts says the company's strategy falls far short of the kind of the tough restructuring it needs.
Moreover, those analysts say, Siemens shares have only risen this year because they lagged so badly last year.

"The recent share price increase doesn't imply that Siemens is undertaking radical strategic overhaul as are some other German corporates," Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Kevin Brau said in a recent research note.

And Brau is not alone. Moody's Investor Service last week cut its rating on Siemens senior debt, saying the company's cost-cutting has been "insufficient" to counter international competition. Moody's also said Siemens exceptional balance sheet strength could deteriorate in the medium term.
"Their restructuring really hasn't gotten them anywhere," said another analyst who did not want to be identified.

Yet Siemens, which reports nine-month results next Monday, has its believers -- and investors. Its shares opened on Wednesday above 115 marks, up from 72 in January. In that time, the German blue-chip DAX index has risen 40 percent, although it has outpaced Siemens in the last 12 months.
"The share has underperformed, and their margins aren't as good as their international competitors'," said one of the optimists, Andreas Wahl, at Credit Lyonnais in Frankfurt.
"But ultimately things are positive," said Wahl, who recently reiterated a "buy" rating on the stock -- meaning that he expected Siemens to beat the market by 10 percent or more.
Wahl based his outlook on the mark's dramatic weakening against the dollar, which lifts Siemens' export strength, as well as recent moves to sell off weaker businesses.
Siemens wants to sell its dental technology and defence electronics businesses as part of a 18-month plan to divest units with turnover of about 3.5 billion marks.
"I think we will see the company making more strenuous efforts to get to 15 percent return on equity," Wahl said.

Much of the pessimism about Siemens stemmed from a warning last fall that profit would not improve this year, largely due to plummeting prices for semiconductors, previously one of its most profitable sectors.

But Brau, who rated Siemens at "hold," said the problems go beyond chip prices, noting that Siemens hasn't pared personnel costs, which amount to 40 percent of sales, versus 28 percent for Swiss-Swedish competitor ABB.

He also would like to see Siemens reorganise into four or five focused companies -- so that investors can buy into high-growth telecommunications, semiconductors, automation and automotive technology units without also getting stakes in mature industrial units like power generation and lighting.
Brau doubted there could be a positive earnings surprise in the nine-month figures on July 21. "Siemens never has any surprises," he told Reuters.
Wahl forecast sales in the nine months to June 30 would rise 5.3 percent to 67.9 billion marks, with net profit increasing two percent to 1.68 billion.

Siemens defends the pace of its restructuring by pointing out that radical change is difficult in Germany. "We couldn't allow mass layoffs, as some people would like," said spokesman Thomas Weber in an interview.
And Siemens' progress was clear -- with an 8.5 percent productivity gain last year, divestments underway, and Asian and American orders rising by double-digit rates, he said.
Moreover, Siemens rules out slimming down to a few operating companies.

"That is our strategic advantage," Weber said. "If we get a contract for a new airport, we can provide the power generation, lighting, telecommunications, the computer systems, the mass transit systems. Nobody else has that."
-- neal.boudette@reuters.com (Bonn +49-228 26097150)
